gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI AC180's solar input is capped at 10 A (12–60 V, 500 W max, DC7909 port). With that cap, the two 200 W panels in the AC180 + 2× 200 W kit give close to their rated 400 W only when wired in series. Wired in parallel, the current cap holds them to about 10 A × panel Vmp, which is roughly 200 W for 20 V-class panels, about half the panels' rating. BLUETTI's manual says panels can go 'in series or parallel' and gives no warning about this.
standout_why: I compared against StormWatts (cited), Volt & Valley's combo page and their search-result pages. StormWatts gives 12–60 V / 20 A / 1,000 W for the Elite 100 V2 and Elite 200 V2 and works out series versus parallel for the Elite 200 V2 with two SP200L panels. It does not give the AC180's input current or cover any AC180 kit wiring. Volt & Valley gives only 'AC180 500W, 2x 220-250W panels', with no voltage or current, and says no station's voltage window is on its page. Following that pairing in parallel would hit the 10 A cap. OutageReady, UnpluggedWatts and our own page would not load because of a TLS error, so I could not check them.
decides: The pick does not change, because the AC180 kits are pre-orders that dispatch Dec 14, 2026 and the pick must ship now. The finding adds a condition to the AC180 + 2× 200 W row ($1,170.40 at the link price, $1,232 store price): it reaches 400 W of solar only in series. Series gives about 49.2 V Voc from two panels at StormWatts' SP200L figure of 24.6 V each, under the 60 V limit. Parallel gives 21.6 A Isc against a 10 A input. By StormWatts' 12–60 V / 20 A figures, the Elite 100 V2 handles 400 W of panels either way, so it is the safer 1 kWh station for a 400 W kit. Note also that our kit table lists 'AC 400 W' for bluetti-ac180-2x200w-solar-kit. The AC180's AC output is 1,800 W, so that cell is an error to fix.

findings.label: Solar (DC) input limits and port
findings.value: 12–60 V Voc, 10 A max, 500 W max; DC7909 interface
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC180 Portable Power Station User Manual (hosted on manuals.plus)
findings.note: From the specs table ('Power: 500W/10A Max.', 'Voltage: 12-60VDC', 'Interface: DC7909') and section 4.3.2 ('Voc: 12V-60V, Input Current: 10A Max., Input Power: 500W Max.'). BLUETTI's own manual PDF (cdn.shopify.com/.../AC180_User_Manual.pdf, dated 2023-06-16) downloaded but its text could not be extracted here, so this mirror was used.

findings.label: Maker's wiring guidance and Voc exclusion
findings.value: 'Connect the solar panels (in series or parallel) to AC180 via the solar charging cable'; 'The open circuit voltage of solar panels cannot exceed 60V, otherwise it will damage the device.'
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC180 Portable Power Station User Manual (hosted on manuals.plus)
findings.note: The manual allows either wiring and says nothing about the 10 A cap limiting parallel strings. Manualslib's copy, p. 3, has the same rule: 'Do not use solar panels with open circuit voltage higher than 60V.' The box includes a 16 AWG, 1,500 mm solar charging cable (p. 9). The AC180P manual says over-60 V damage is not covered by warranty, but I only saw that in a search snippet and did not open it.

findings.label: Wiring arithmetic for the 400 W kit on a 10 A input
findings.value: Series: about 49.2 V Voc and 10.8 A Isc, within 12–60 V. Parallel: about 21.6 A Isc against a 10 A cap, so about 10 A × panel Vmp, roughly 200 W from 400 W of panels
findings.source_title: Solar Generator Kits Compared at the Same Panel Watts | StormWatts
findings.note: Panel figures are StormWatts' BLUETTI SP200L values (Voc 24.6 V, Isc 10.8 A); the station limits are from the AC180 manual above. Series Voc = 2 × 24.6 = 49.2 V; parallel Isc = 2 × 10.8 = 21.6 A. StormWatts estimates about 56.5 V at −4°F for two SP200L in series, still under 60 V. This is arithmetic at rated values, not a measurement. I could not confirm on a BLUETTI page that the AC180 kit's 200 W panel is the SP200L.
